Per-service ranges vary — for example, board-up services run $300–$900, soot removal $1,000–$4,000, and a kitchen fire $2,000–$8,000. An exact quote needs a free on-site assessment.
faqs.q: How much does fire damage restoration cost?

faqs.a: Most Texas HO-3 homeowner policies cover sudden and accidental fire damage, including smoke and water damage from firefighting. You have the right to choose your own restoration contractor — your insurer cannot force you to use their preferred vendor. Document everything before cleanup begins, notify your insurer within 24–48 hours, and keep receipts for board-up, temporary housing, and meals — Additional Living Expenses (ALE) coverage usually reimburses these.
faqs.q: Will my homeowner's insurance cover fire damage in Texas?

texas_fire_facts: Texas consistently ranks among the top states for residential structure fires. Cooking is the leading cause of home fires statewide. Spring severe-weather season brings lightning-strike fires; winter cold snaps bring heating-equipment and space-heater fires. West and Central Texas face recurring wildfire risk in dry years. Texas structure fires cause more than $800M in property losses per year, with ~20,000 structure fires reported statewide in 2023 (Texas Fire Incident Reporting System).

texas_insurance_playbook.license_note: Texas does not require a general state contractor license for restoration work. Verify local city permits for structural repair. Always confirm the contractor carries general liability and workers comp insurance.
points: Most Texas HO-3 homeowner policies cover sudden and accidental fire damage, including smoke and water damage from firefighting.
You have the right to choose your own restoration contractor — your insurer cannot force you to use their preferred vendor.
Document everything before cleanup begins: photos/video of every room, list of damaged contents.
Most policies require prompt notice — call your insurer within 24-48 hours of the fire.
Keep receipts for emergency board-up, temporary housing, and meals — Additional Living Expenses (ALE) coverage usually reimburses these.
Do not sign over your full claim check or sign an Assignment of Benefits without understanding it — get the scope in writing first.
